conviction_note: Scale is the 13.4% event-implied move (wide 62% ATM spread) against a 12.5% median reaction, so abs_move 13.5. The negative lean comes from European gas doubling since O-I last spoke (TTF ~EUR45 June avg to EUR82-91 Sep-Oct) on the 20-25% of 2026 gas that is unhedged and the roughly half of 2027 that is unhedged, after two straight guide cuts and two -15% reactions. Ardagh's Q3 confirms European overcapacity and a weak North America. Offsets: strong Americas margins, Constellation beer shipments up 5.5%, and Ardagh closing furnaces. The skew (+9.9 downside paid) already agrees with the negative, and the bar is unsourced ($0.03 vs $0.05 EPS, no EBITDA consensus), so p_up is held at 44 rather than lower. The findings sum (-1.2) and the scaled number (-1.6) agree in sign and size.
bar: Unsourced and disputed. Consensus Q3 EPS is $0.03 on one aggregator and $0.05 on another (earningswhispers / unusualwhales, https://unusualwhales.com/stock/OI/earnings), and revenue estimates range $1.52-1.64B across aggregator pages. O-I withdrew EPS guidance in July because of a 40-70% tax rate, so EPS is near noise. The operative bar is the company FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide of $1.0-1.1B (cut from $1.125-1.225B), FCF a use of $50-150M, leverage at or slightly above 4x, and the 2027 EBITDA target of $1.2-1.3B (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000812074/000110465926087559/tm2621494d1_ex99-1.htm, 2026-07-28). No Q3 EBITDA consensus was found, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 13.9M shares, 4.6 days to cover, at the 2026-08-14 settlement, up from 11.8M / 3.2 days on 07-31 (curvedtrading via search snippet; the page returned 403). Fintel (undated) gives 9.23% of float and 7.53 days; equibles (Aug 19) gives 7.7% of float and 3.2 days. That is moderate, not crowded, and no October settlement was found. Skew is +9.93 vol points (downside paid); put/call OI is 0.83 with total OI only 4,272. Run-up is +13.1% over 20 days and +7.95% over 5 days off a 2026-09-22 one-year low; the stock is still -61.6% from its 52-week high. Citi upgraded to Buy in late August with a 90-day upside catalyst watch that spans this print.

findings.finding: European gas has nearly doubled since O-I last guided, and its hedge cover leaves part of Q4 2026 and about half of 2027 exposed. TTF front-month futures were EUR82-82.5/MWh on 10-14 Sep 2026 and about EUR89-91 on 22 Oct 2026, against a June 2026 average of EUR44.94. O-I said in April it had locked 75-80% of 2026 European gas, with more than 50% mitigated for 2027. In July it cut FY26 EBITDA to $1.0-1.1B, partly on European energy costs, with Europe segment profit at $6M (0.9% margin) in Q2. The market expects Europe to improve sequentially in H2, as management said; the risk is a third guide cut, or the low end of the range, plus pressure on the 2027 $1.2-1.3B target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance was cut in April (energy-driven, pre-announced around Apr 10) and again in July; the prints of 2026-04-28 and 2026-07-28 each moved about -15% (baseline). The 2025-11-04 print, without a cut, was +14%.
findings.why_not_priced: The gas spike is public, but the company has not spoken since July 28, when TTF was about EUR50-60; no Q3 EBITDA consensus or post-September estimate revision was found. If it were fully priced, the stock would not have rallied 13% in 20 days into the print. The +9.9 skew suggests part of it is priced.
findings.independence: The hedge figures come from O-I's own Q1 release and call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/30/o-i-glass-oi-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). The October TTF level (~EUR91, 22 Oct) is from a separate source: https://en.apa.az/energy-and-industry/gas-prices-in-europe-exceed-1050-for-first-time-since-december-2022-531675. Verallia makes its 2026 outlook conditional on no significant Middle East deterioration (https://www.abcbourse.com/marches/verallia-maintient-ses-objectifs-2026-apres-un-premier-semestre-resilient_700502). This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has confirmed as a mechanism but not quantified at current prices.

findings.finding: Ardagh Glass Packaging's Q3 2026 (published 2026-10-23, after O-I last spoke) shows glass adjusted EBITDA down 6% at constant currency to $179M, worldwide shipments down 1%, and North America shipments down 6%. This is a weak read for North American glass demand in the quarter O-I reports, where O-I's Americas tons were already down 7% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: O-I's Americas tons fell 7% in Q2 2026, yet segment profit rose 22% on Fit to Win; Americas volume misses have mattered less than European profit on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out four days before the print, and O-I trades on a 20-day run-up of +13%, which does not look like a market leaning into a weak Americas volume quarter. Net of the rest: O-I's Americas margin gained 300bp in Q2 on cost, and its North American mix (spirits, food, Mexico beer) differs from Ardagh's US beer-heavy book, so the read-through is partial.
findings.independence: This finding and the next share one document (the Ardagh Q3 release). Constellation's beer shipments (next findings) point the other way for O-I's Mexican beer glass.

findings.finding: Ardagh (published 2026-10-23) cited 'surplus production capacity across Europe' and proposed decommissioning a furnace at each of Holmegaard (Denmark) and Knottingley (UK), after closing Germersheim in Q3 2026. This is competitor capacity leaving the European container-glass market, where O-I's Q2 Europe prices fell 4% on competitive pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior O-I print has reacted to competitor capacity cuts in the baseline; Europe price and cost has been the line of the last two -15% reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is four days old. If management frames European supply rationalisation as supporting 2027 pricing on the Oct 28 call, it addresses the line the stock has sold off on. The +7.95% 5-day run-up may already partly reflect it.
findings.independence: Same document as the Ardagh North America finding. Separately, Verallia cited restructuring charges for 'industrial footprint adaptation' in Europe in H1 2026 (https://www.optionfinance.fr/info-financiere-en-continu/d/2026-07-29-le-benefice-net-de-verallia-greve-par-des-charges-de-restructuration.html).

findings.finding: Constellation Brands' beer shipments rose about 5.5% in its fiscal Q2 (June-August 2026) while depletions fell 0.6%, as it rebuilt distributor inventory; management said September depletions improved. This is a demand proxy for Mexican beer-bottle glass in O-I's Americas segment during the quarter being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Americas profit grew 22% in Q2 2026 on cost, while the stock fell 15% on Europe; Americas strength alone has not been enough to lift a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Constellation reported after O-I's July call. O-I said in July that volumes were improving through the quarter and expected H2 growth; a restocking shipment bump at a large beer customer supports that. It is a proxy: O-I's share of Constellation's glass is not quantified here.
findings.independence: Proxy. The O-I-Constellation supply relationship is not confirmed in a document fetched here. The Ardagh North America -6% points the other way.

findings.finding: Management's own H2 set-up: in July it said Europe should improve sequentially through H2; that $115-120M of Fit to Win savings is targeted for H2, with just under half already locked in and $200M or more for FY26; and that new contracted business adds 1-1.5% to the run rate in H2, with easier comparisons. These sit inside the July guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: O-I has missed its own H2-recovery framing twice in 2026 (April and July cuts), each followed by about -15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: this is the company's own guided path, so it is sized close to zero. It is filed because delivery of the locked-in savings would steady the Americas line.
findings.independence: The same figures are in the Q2 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000812074/000110465926087559/tm2621494d1_ex99-1.htm

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +14% on 2025-11-04 came from a depressed base, which is the closest analogue to a relief rally.

findings.why_not_priced: Short interest of about 8-9% of float is moderate: it could add to a relief move on an in-line guide, but it is not a crowded squeeze set-up. The 20-day run-up raises the bar slightly. Net small positive.
findings.independence: The short interest series (curvedtrading via snippet; fintel https://fintel.io/s/us/OI) is a different source from the Citi note.

findings.finding: European pricing pressure continues at peers: Verallia's H1 2026 revenue fell 1.4% on lower sales prices, and its Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 21.4% from 22.5%. This is consistent with O-I's -4% Europe price in Q2 and suggests no near-term price recovery to offset energy costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: European price and cost drove the -15% reactions in April and July 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it was published the same day as O-I's Q2. Verallia's Q3 2026 release was not found, so there is no fresher peer read. Filed small.
findings.independence: O-I's own Q2 Europe price (-4%) in the 8-K says the same thing; this is partly overlapping evidence, sized small accordingly.

outside_window.finding: The EU ban on Russian LNG imports from 2027-01-01 and a winter TTF forecast of EUR85 (Morgan Stanley) bear on O-I's 2027 European energy cost, of which only about half is hedged. The 2027 cost lands after the window, though any 2027 commentary on the Oct 28 call is inside it and is covered by finding 1.

baseline_tension: The net negative lean agrees with the +9.9 put skew and the last two -15% prints, but cuts against the +13% 20-day / +8% 5-day run-up off a September low, so the negative is probably partly priced and p_up is held at 44 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign agrees with a strong skew, so likely partly priced) and rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission): energy finding shrunk from -3.0 to -2.5.

Rule 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest of the company): Ardagh North America read shrunk from -1.0 to -0.8, because O-I's Americas mix differs from Ardagh's and its margin gains are cost-driven.
Rule 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): all sizes kept small, and p_up moved from 42 to 44.
Short interest is about 8-9% of float, not crowded, so no squeeze cut was applied beyond the small positive positioning finding.
